links.evidence: npz_exporter is described as responsible for segmentation, short-segment polyline merging, fitting, sampling, and final NPZ fields.
The core exporter centrally handles fiber cut among other events.
Offline expansion supplies the lift, remaining wait, and retract that allow UART cut handling to be nonblocking online.
README says the UART cut path relies on offline NPZ expansion for lift, wait, and safety retract.
GCode CUT maps to cut and is then expanded by the shared exporter into nonblocking cut event, lift, wait, and retract.
GCode CLI cut_lift_mm and cut_wait_s correspond to the exporter lift distance and wait duration.
gcode_planner parses into path_processing_core.types and calls export_npz to generate the system NPZ.
Top-level README summarizes the same short-segment POLYLINE continuous sampling rule defined in the core README.
The rule avoids repeated independent acceleration and deceleration around tiny segments and local stalls.
The GCode exporter path says short segments are sampled as original POLYLINE while normal long paths use B-splines.
external_npz_preprocessor does not directly write system NPZ and delegates final output to export_npz.
The preprocessor leaves cut event generation, Z lift, wait fill, safety retract, offsets, and NPZ fields to the core exporter.
The parameter model says dt, tool_offset, resin_z_print_compensation_mm, cut lift/wait, and offsets are passed to export_npz.
The shared exporter keeps short-segment polyline sampling centralized for external NPZ conversion.
cut_lift_mm and cut_wait_s are documented as forwarded values that control the exporter cut expansion.
Source NPZ fiber paths emit only semantic CUT; export_npz generates the actual cut event, lift, wait, and retract.
Formal UI sends GCode files through gcode_planner.gcode_parser before export.
Formal UI sends agreed-format NPZ inputs through external_npz_preprocessor.
UI routes both adapters to export_npz, collecting parameters and offset consistency without duplicating export logic.
UI exposes cut_lift_mm and cut_wait_s but explicitly does not expand cut lift, wait, or retract itself.
